Hi everyone, here's a quick summary of where we are this week. The dictation app is now stable for daily use, and the median time from releasing the key to seeing the text is about one and a half seconds. The biggest delay comes from long dictations, because we only start transcribing after you let go. Next, we're going to transcribe while you speak, so that only the last few seconds are left at the end. We're also testing a smaller version of the Hindi model, which should make short dictations faster. If you have feedback, please reply in the thread or send me a direct message.

Hi Mark, thanks for your time on the call yesterday. As discussed, we'll start with a two week pilot for your support team, beginning on Monday, the first of December. During the pilot, we'll set up the app on ten laptops, run a short training session, and collect feedback at the end of each week. The pilot is free, and if you decide to continue, we'll send a proposal with annual pricing. Could you please send me the names and email addresses of the people who will take part? Let me know if you have any questions.

So the way the new pipeline works is fairly simple. While you're holding the key, the app keeps listening for short pauses in your speech. Every time it finds one, it sends the audio before that pause to the speech model in the background. By the time you let go, most of your dictation has already been transcribed, and only the last part is left. The tricky part is choosing where to cut. If we cut in the middle of a word, the model gets confused, so we only cut when there's at least half a second of silence. We also cut anyway after about twenty five seconds, because the model reads thirty seconds at a time.
